messages.content: Can we finish San Antonio airfare today? Please compare the United nonstop pair I was leaning toward with the cheaper connecting option. I need Tuesday bag-drop time before the early-evening welcome, no rental car, and a Thursday return after lunch.

I rechecked the two live options:

| Option | Fare | Tue arrival/buffer | Thu return | Transfer assumption | Trade-off |
| United nonstop ORD-SAT | $352 | 12:50-3:46; rideshare to Hampton about 18-22 min, so hotel by about 4:25 | 2:05-4:57 ORD; about 80-90 min airport margin after noon wrap-up and bag pickup | SAT rideshare about $20-25 each way | Smoothest; no connection risk |
| Lower fare with connection | $279 | 10:35-3:25 via Dallas, 52-min connection; hotel about 4:05 if on time | 3:20-8:08 ORD via Houston | Same local transfer | Saves $73, but delay risk could cut into the welcome and gets you home much later |

With the $397 Hampton hold, United puts the defensible trip estimate around $799 before meals; the connection is about $726. I would ticket United unless the $73 savings is important.
If the outbound into Dallas is late, is there a backup that still gets me to the welcome?

Not a comfortable one. The next reaccommodation path I see lands after 5:15-5:45, which would leave no real hotel buffer before the welcome. The return connection is less mission-critical, but it is why the Chicago arrival slips past 8. United’s nonstop mainly buys schedule certainty.
Any Southwest from Midway that beats this without the connection?

No nonstop from Midway in this scan. The best Southwest fare is $301 with Dallas both ways: similar connection exposure, a 4:15 p.m. San Antonio arrival Tuesday, and a 7:50 p.m. Chicago arrival Thursday. Carry-on only helps; it does not remove the timing risk.
Okay, please ticket the United economy fare, not basic economy. Use the same traveler details and Known Traveler number.

Ticketed: United economy ORD-SAT Tue Jan. 23, 12:50 p.m.-3:46 p.m.; SAT-ORD Thu Jan. 25, 2:05 p.m.-4:57 p.m. Fare charged: $352. Seat selection is included, and the Known Traveler number is attached. San Antonio is now Hampton Riverwalk Jan. 23-25 at about $397, plus rideshares and no rental car. I will keep the Thursday noon wrap-up assumption flagged in case the organizer changes it.

messages.content: Quick San Antonio check: the organizer added an optional Thursday roundtable that may run to 12:35. The Hampton confirmed early breakfast, fridge, and bag storage. With my 2:05 United return, do I need the later nonstop, or can I keep this?

If you stay until 12:35, it is snug but workable with only a rollaboard: leave venue 12:35, hotel bag pickup by 12:45-12:50, rideshare to SAT 15-20 min, airport about 1:05-1:10 for the 2:05. The later nonstop is 5:25-8:18 p.m. ORD and about +$96.
I can slip out at 12:20 if it is still going. I would rather not get home after 8.

Keep the booked 2:05. Use breakfast, check out before the program, leave bags at Hampton, and call the rideshare no later than 12:45. If the roundtable becomes mandatory past 12:30, revisit; otherwise no flight change is needed.

messages.content: I’m starting the Baltimore site visit. Dates are Feb. 22-24 from Chicago. Wednesday is a 9 a.m. meeting near the central library, then an afternoon partner visit in Station North. Thursday debrief should end before noon. Please compare BWI versus other airport options and hotels near the library versus Inner Harbor. No rental car; breakfast, room coffee, and a fridge would be helpful if practical.
Got it. Should I include both ORD and Midway, and is there a nightly hotel cap or reimbursement line I should keep in mind?
Use either airport, economy. Hotel guidance is roughly under $230 before tax, refundable preferred. Tuesday arrival should leave time for dinner and prep, not a late-night arrival.

Here is the compact scan.

Flights:
| Option | Fare | Timing | Ground plan | Trade-off |
| United ORD-BWI | $312 | Tue 10:45-1:35; Thu 2:40-3:55 ORD | BWI rideshare to downtown about 25 min, $30-40 | Best return margin after debrief; assigned seat with standard economy |
| Southwest MDW-BWI | $266 | Tue 9:55-12:40; Thu 1:55-3:05 MDW | Same BWI transfer; checked bags included | Cheaper, but less margin Thursday and no assigned seat |
| American ORD-DCA | $244 | Tue 11:30-2:20; Thu 2:15-3:35 ORD | DCA to Baltimore is 75-95 min by rail transfers or a costly rideshare | Fare looks good, but ground time erases most savings |

Hotels for Feb. 22-24:
| Hotel | Est. total | Meeting access | Breakfast/room amenities | Dining/cancel terms |
| Hotel Revival Mount Vernon | $458 | Closest: about 6-8 min walk to central library; short ride to Station North | Breakfast not included; room coffee listed; mini-fridge by request | On-site restaurant; refundable about 48 hrs out |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Inner Harbor | $336 | 7-10 min rideshare or about 20 min walk to library | Breakfast included; in-room coffee and mini-fridge listed | Many restaurants nearby; cancel by evening Feb. 21 |
| Staybridge Suites Inner Harbor | $374 | Similar ride to library | Breakfast included; kitchenette with coffee maker and full fridge | No full restaurant, but nearby dining; cancel by Feb. 20 |

BWI is the practical airport. For hotel value, Hampton Inner Harbor is the cleanest balance; the Revival is easier on Wednesday morning but costs about $120 more.
Is DCA worth keeping in the mix if the American fare drops below $240?

Probably not unless it drops by at least $90-$100 compared with BWI. The rail transfer from DCA to Baltimore adds time and complexity, and a direct rideshare can eat the fare savings quickly. BWI is simpler for a no-car trip.
Then keep BWI. Between United and Southwest, which is less awkward if the Thursday debrief runs closer to noon?

United is less awkward. With the 2:40 p.m. BWI departure, you could leave a noon debrief, retrieve bags, and still reach BWI around 1:15-1:25. The 1:55 Southwest return works if everything ends on time, but it leaves less slack. The United premium is $46.
Let’s lean United, then. For hotels, can you verify breakfast is actually included at Hampton and Staybridge, and whether rooms have in-room coffee and a fridge? I do not want lobby coffee only.

Confirmed from the current listings: Hampton Inner Harbor lists free hot breakfast, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, and microwave in the standard king and two-queen rooms. Staybridge lists breakfast included plus an in-suite coffee maker and full refrigerator/kitchenette. Revival has the better on-site restaurant and location, but breakfast is not included and the fridge is a request rather than a guaranteed standard amenity.
How much extra local transit am I buying if I choose Hampton instead of Revival?

Roughly $40-$55 total. Wednesday: Hampton to the library about $10-$14 by rideshare, library to Station North about $10, Station North back to Hampton about $12-$15. Thursday depends on the debrief location, but assume another $10-$14. The hotel savings versus Revival is still about $120, so Hampton remains ahead.
Any concern about dinner Tuesday? I may just want something easy after landing.

Hampton is fine for that. It does not have a full restaurant, but there are casual dinner choices within a few blocks toward the Inner Harbor and Harbor East. I would use main streets and a short rideshare if you are tired after dark. Revival wins on having an on-site restaurant; Hampton wins on total cost and breakfast.
Can you also check cancellation terms and one-bed availability for Hampton? Queen is fine; king is fine if that is the cheaper one.

Hampton has a refundable standard king at $336 total, cancel by 6 p.m. local time on Feb. 21. Two queens are available at about $348 total with the same terms. The standard king is the better hold. I can add a quiet-room, away-from-elevator request.
Let’s put Hampton Inner Harbor on hold, standard king if that is the $336 one, quiet away from the elevator. Do not ticket flights yet; I want to confirm the Thursday debrief time.

Held: Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor, Feb. 22-24, refundable standard king, estimated $336 with taxes. Quiet room away from elevator requested. Breakfast, in-room coffee, mini-fridge, and microwave are listed. Flights are not ticketed; United ORD-BWI is the leading option for the return margin.
Before you close it, what is the full expected total with United plus that hotel and normal rideshares?

Working estimate: United airfare $312 + Hampton $336 + BWI airport rideshares about $70 + local rideshares about $45 = about $763 before meals. Southwest would make it about $717 but with a tighter Thursday return. Revival plus United would be around $840 after lower local transit, so Hampton/United is the better value.
Good. Please save that as the working plan and remind me what remains open.

Saved as the Baltimore working plan: BWI airport, no rental car, Hampton Inner Harbor standard king held Feb. 22-24 at about $336, quiet-room request attached, and United ORD-BWI as the leading flight pair. Still open: confirm the exact Thursday debrief end time and location, then ticket either United or another BWI option if fares shift.
